minutes.headline: School Committee held a facilitated workshop reviewing its roles and operating protocols; no formal votes were taken.
minutes.summary: A facilitator led the committee through a review of governance roles and a start/stop/continue exercise on how the board works. Members discussed public comment rules, social media, open meeting law, community engagement, and adding student-achievement presentations to agendas. A resident commented at the end on the cost of "free" public education to families.

public_comment.topic: Resident said the workshop was valuable, urged professional advice on community engagement and communications, and read a log of fees his family has paid for 'free' public education this school year.

votes.motion: Motion to adjourn (heard as 'motion for journal')

budget_items.topic: Family costs of public education fees
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident listed fees his family has paid so far for the coming school year and estimated the yearly total, arguing that costs to families are not insignificant.

budget_items.topic: Funding for curriculum director and town planning
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said the town plans adding firefighters and police but the schools cannot plan a curriculum director because they are always treading water; wants to meet town officials on funding.
The superintendent said last year's budget forced a choice between maintaining programs and avoiding large first-grade classes.

decisions.decision: Agreed to read the mission statement at the opening of each meeting / put it on the agenda.
Agreed to add student and department presentations early on the agenda, before the work session and after public comment, with time limits.
Agreed to revisit the operating protocols periodically, perhaps in the winter.
Agreed to edit protocols to add deliberating to the open meeting law communication language and to state the per-person public comment limit.

what_happened.line: The School Committee held a facilitated workshop on its roles and operating protocols and took no formal votes.
Members agreed to edit the protocols to add deliberating to the open meeting law language and to state a per-person public comment limit.
Members agreed to read the mission statement at the opening of each meeting and put it on the agenda.
Members agreed to add student and department presentations early on the agenda, after public comment, with time limits.
A resident told the committee that fees his family has paid for 'free' public education are not insignificant.

why_it_matters: The changes set how residents can speak at School Committee meetings and how much of each agenda goes to student work and presentations.

Members also raised how last year's school budget forced a choice between programs and class size, and how schools could plan a curriculum director, which bears on future budget requests and the fees families pay.
watch_next: The committee said it would revisit the operating protocols periodically, perhaps in the winter, and the edited protocols would be the document to check.
